 Korean media reports suggest that Vietnam is becoming a key market for K-pop idols.
 From BigBang and Blackpink to veteran groups and new-generation idols, Vietnam is increasingly asserting its appeal on the K-pop performance map.
 Báo Lao Động • 27/10/2026 Follow Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e Add Vietnam.vn on G o o g l e 0 
 Vietnam is becoming a key market for K-pop idols. Photo: Duong Huong 
 BigBang 's two concerts at My Dinh National Stadium ( Hanoi ) on October 24-25 attracted approximately 80,000 spectators. This was BigBang's first solo concert in Vietnam since their debut in 2006. 
 Following the announcement of the concert, searches for Hanoi tourism increased approximately fourfold. The Hanoi Tourism Association predicts that the event will attract 175,000-190,000 visitors, generating tourism revenue of 650-800 billion VND. 
 On South Korean online communities, Koreans were also amazed by the generosity and enthusiasm of Vietnamese fans. 
 A destination for both veteran idols and new-generation groups. 
 According to Chosun, Vietnam previously did not receive as much attention in the Asian K-pop market compared to Japan, China, Indonesia, or English-speaking countries like the Philippines and Singapore . 
 However, increased investment from South Korean businesses, along with a significant rise in the number of Vietnamese students studying in South Korea, has boosted cultural exchange between the two countries. Since 2020, Vietnam has gradually become an important market for K-pop. 
 You may also like Korean media noted that in the 2010s, Vietnam was considered a familiar performance destination for idols past their peak. However, nowadays, veteran artists who maintain their appeal, along with popular male and female groups, are including Vietnam in their schedules. 
 In 2023, Blackpink held two concerts in Hanoi, attracting approximately 67,000 attendees. In 2024, artists such as Baekhyun, Kim Jae Joong, Park Bom, and Chanyeol will come to Vietnam to perform solo. 
 In 2025, 2NE1 returned to the stage in Ho Chi Minh City with their full lineup after 11 years, while Tiffany (SNSD) held her own concert. G-Dragon's concert also attracted approximately 100,000 spectators over two days of performances in Hung Yen . 
 This year, T-ara, EXO, and TVXQ's Yunho also came to Vietnam to perform. These names show that the market's appeal comes not only from young audiences but also from fans who have followed K-pop for generations. 
 At the BigBang concert, many middle-aged audience members still showed special affection for the group after nearly two decades. Meanwhile, younger audiences also continued to find common ground with BigBang's music. 
 BigBang had two explosive concerts at My Dinh Stadium on the evenings of October 24th and 25th. Photo: Duong Huong 
 The performing arts market is receiving increasing attention. 
 You may also like The growth of the Vietnamese market is causing the South Korean music industry to change its approach. 
 Yoon Hwi, chairman of Carpa, a South Korean-owned business in Vietnam that co-organized the BigBang concert with VPBank and other partners, commented: “Compared to the appeal of K-pop, Vietnam used to be on the sidelines of the performing arts industry. But in just a few years, this market has developed rapidly and become one of the K-pop concert hubs in Southeast Asia.” 
 This prospect is further demonstrated by upcoming events. In January 2027, the Golden Disc Awards, a South Korean music awards ceremony, is expected to be held in Hanoi for the first time. Plans to bring the girl group IVE to perform in Vietnam in April 2027 are also underway. 
 Popular music critic Lim Hee Yoon argues that the strength of the Southeast Asian market lies in the fact that multiple generations share a love for K-pop. It's not just adult audiences who followed the first generation of idols; fans in their 10s and 20s also show great interest in this genre. 
 The combination of a large fanbase, concert spending power, and tourism potential is making Vietnam an increasingly important destination in the international performance strategies of K-pop artists.
